name: Selegiline
mechanism: Selective irreversible monoamine oxidase-B inhibitor at therapeutic doses
dosing: Typically 5 mg twice daily (oral preparations); dosing varies with formulation
contraindications: Concurrent use with meperidine, SSRIs, SNRIs, MAO inhibitors; uncontrolled hypertension
interactions: Serotonergic drugs (serotonin syndrome risk), sympathomimetics; avoid amphetamines
sideEffects: Insomnia (more common with transdermal/patch), nausea, dizziness, orthostatic hypotension, hallucinations
clinicalPearls: Often used as adjunct in Parkinson's disease; watch for interactions with antidepressants.
